reviewed_by: Codex shared-budget and per-host CPU policy coverage review; independent causal validators recorded in docs/validation/host-cpu-budget.md
reason: One Core coordinator delegates pure PDF layout to an explicitly injected bounded process pool. An added held-close worker teardown regression covers concurrent crash/shutdown cleanup. Selected pool/report/harness cases cover process/loop/context ownership, FIFO and count/byte admission, cancellation, worker recovery, PDF equivalence/artifact integrity/cache/revision/auth and preserved tool ledgers. Butler coverage proves fresh authenticated host-load reads, shared off-loop sampling, unknown values, discovery/help/catalog, source digest and actual startup Chroma synchronization. The 16 model boundary cases cover fairness, admission, byte limits, cancellation, failure/shutdown, RPC framing, harness rollover identity, bounded recorded polling retries, unretried ordinary reads, live grow/drain and both inert-executor startup paths. Sixteen host CPU policy cases cover per-host persistence/project sharing, observed application/retry, automatic/custom validation, identity/revision conflicts, restart, capacity reduction, corrupt-policy degradation and Butler read/save/readback. Product help includes CPU configuration discovery. Exactly 106 Python cases on 3.11/3.12/3.13 and 62 frontend cases in four feature-specific files are selected. Browser acceptance is exactly one real-Core CPU Settings journey in each of eight permanent desktop/compact/Chromium mobile/WebKit mobile profiles: pairing, save/reload, conflict/retry, observed/inactive state, accessibility and touch geometry. The separate owned-LAN model verifies actual kernel limits with 50 synthetic Core chats and ordinary HTTP/Butler reads. No full suite is selected.
exclusions: No full suites. Host CPU policy, existing pool/report/harness boundaries and per-host control/receipt/discovery are selected. The browser matrix is one CPU Settings journey in eight profiles; unrelated interface journeys are excluded after review of the scoped card/CSS insertion. Real provider/GPU work, production deployment and native/frozen executor activation are excluded. The shared executor remains inactive in ordinary Core startup; saving its policy does not enable it.
